summary.en: Gold smuggling is now reported to be financing an Islamic State-linked insurgency in eastern DRC, with gold flowing through Uganda to support rebels, according to Sentry. Ebola cases have surpassed 10,000 and a nurse treating patients was killed by a mob, while a health worker was wounded, prompting Uganda to tighten its border. Rebel forces continue to capture weapons from fleeing DRC and Burundian troops and the DRC army has recaptured strategic territory from a rebel group led by an ex-president. The conflict produced 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Gullsmugling skal nå ifølge Sentry finansiere en IS-tilknyttet opprør i Øst-DRC, med gull som strømmer gjennom Uganda for å støtte opprørerne. Ebola-tilfeller har passert 10 000, og en sykepleier som behandlet pasienter ble drept av en mobb, mens en helsearbeider ble såret, noe som får Uganda til å stramme inn grensen. Opprørsstyrker fortsetter å ta våpen fra flyktende DRC‑ og burundiske tropper, og DRC-hæren har gjenerobret strategisk territorium fra en opprørsgruppe ledet av en tidligere president. Konflikten ga 1 158 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
